### workspace workflow
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
Missing subcommand: list, show, validate, add, update, remove, install, uninstall, run, start, render, check, simulate, status, events, files, attempts, audit, stats, compare, sweep, resume, cancel, approve or reject.

Usage: workspace workflow list [--json]
       workspace workflow uninstall [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow show [ID] [--source] [--json]
       workspace workflow validate PATH|- [--id ID] [--json]
       workspace workflow add ID PATH|- [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow update ID PATH|- --if-sha256 SHA [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow remove ID [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow install [--source N] [--json]
       workspace workflow run ID [--name WORKSPACE] [--input KEY=VALUE]... [--note TEXT] [--pane PANE] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow render ID STEP [--input KEY=VALUE]... [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace workflow check ID STEP [--artifacts DIR] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace workflow simulate ID --script FILE [--input KEY=VALUE]... [--json]
       workspace workflow start --ref REF [--force] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow start [ID] [REF | --prompt TEXT] [--branch BRANCH] [--slug] [--base REF] [--input KEY=VALUE]... [--note TEXT] [--agent-kind KIND] [--[no-]headless] [--prompt-timeout DURATION] [--force] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow status [RUN | --name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME] | --all] [--table] [--json]
       workspace workflow status --needs-me [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace workflow attempts RUN [--attempt-of STEP] [--json]
       workspace workflow audit RUN [--attempt-of STEP] [--json]
       workspace workflow stats ID [--last DURATION] [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace workflow compare ID [--by definition | --by pack:NAME] [--last DURATION] [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace workflow sweep [RUN | --name WORKSPACE] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow sweep --install | --uninstall [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace workflow sweep --installed [--json]
       workspace workflow events RUN [--since N] [--json]
       workspace workflow files RUN [--json]
       workspace workflow resume RUN [--from STEP] [--note TEXT] [--pane PANE] [--extra-attempts N] [--extra-tokens N] [--json]
       workspace workflow cancel RUN [--json]
       workspace workflow approve RUN [--step STEP [--attempt N]] [--note-sha256 HEX] [--note TEXT] [--json]
       workspace workflow reject RUN --note TEXT [--step STEP [--attempt N]] [--to STEP] [--extra-attempts N] [--extra-tokens N] [--json]

Run a workflow in a workspace: an ordered list of steps, each done by the agent in the
workspace's Claude pane. A step gets its instructions in a file under .workflow/ in the
checkout and one typed line pointing at it, in a fresh conversation unless the step says
context: continue. A step is done when the agent's turn ends, every file it produces:
is there (a non-empty regular file, not a link), and its status: check passes; the agent daemon (agentd) sees the turn end and
moves the run on. A failed step goes back along its on_fail: {goto, max}; a step with
gate: approve waits for `workflow approve`. Resources a step uses: are locks the run
holds, in the same queue as `lock acquire` and `dev up`.

Definitions are YAML files: $HOME/.config/workspace/workflows/ID.yml (a project's own, in $HOME/.config/workspace/projects/NAME/workflows/ID.yml, are found first; never read from a repository), then the directories of the workflows.sources config key in list order (source:1, source:2, ...), then the presets that
ship with workspace (rpiv: research, plan, implement, verify; rpiv-auto-approve: rpiv with reviewer agents in place of the plan gate; pr-feedback: triage review feedback, then fix; investigate: reproduce, diagnose, fix; explore: read-only research, a gate, then a report note). See docs/README.workflow.md.

  list       List the workflow definitions in a table (id, source, description)
  uninstall  Remove every workflow installed from the workflows.sources entries
  show       Print one workflow (its inputs and steps)
  validate   Check a definition's text and list every problem
  add        Save a definition as ID.yml
  update     Replace your ID.yml if it is unchanged since you read it
  remove     Delete your ID.yml
  install    Fetch and check the workflows.sources definitions
  run        Start a run of a workflow in a workspace
  render     Print the instructions a step's agent would be sent, without a run
  check      Run one step's status: check once, without a run
  simulate   Play a workflow through the real engine with a scripted fake agent and print the transitions
  start      Make a workspace from a ticket, pull request or prompt and run a workflow in it
  status     Show the runs still going, each with its step and why it is stuck
  attempts   Show what a run recorded about each attempt
  audit      Check a run's kept evidence against the hashes recorded for it
  stats      Show how each step of a workflow went across its runs
  compare    Set a workflow's runs side by side, grouped by definition or pack text
  sweep      One pass over the runs going: act on the ones that have stopped
  events     Show a run's history, one line per event
  files      List the files a run keeps
  resume     Get a run going again
  cancel     End a run and release the locks it holds
  approve    Pass a run's gate
  reject     Turn a run's gate down
Run `workspace workflow VERB --help` for a verb's options.

approve and reject with --step (and --attempt) are refused with gate_not_waiting unless the run
waits at that step's gate (on that attempt), so a stale button can't pass a later gate. These
checks guard against mistakes; they are not a security boundary (docs/README.workflow.md).

`workflow advance RUN [--turn-ended --pane ID [--turn-started AT] [--stopped-at AT] [--background-task TYPE:ID]...]` is what the agent daemon runs to move a run
on when a turn ends; it is not meant to be typed.

`run` and `start` really start a run (start also makes a worktree); --dry-run checks and starts nothing.
`start` may leave out the ID: config names it (workflows.by_ref.<kind>, else workflows.default).
RUN is a workflow run id (see `workspace workflow status`).

        --name WORKSPACE             run: the workspace to run in; render, check: the workspace whose packs and commands are read; show, validate, render, check, simulate, add, update, remove: the workspace whose project's definitions are read first (default: the current workspace); status: that workspace's runs still going (default: the current workspace); sweep: only that workspace's runs (default: every run going)
        --input KEY=VALUE            run, start, render, simulate: a value for one of the workflow's inputs (repeatable)
        --artifacts DIR              check: an existing directory standing for the run's artifacts (WORKSPACE_RUN_ARTIFACTS); default an empty temporary one
        --note TEXT                  run, start: added to every step's instructions; resume, approve, reject: to the next attempt's
        --pane PANE                  run, resume: the pane to run in (%19 or 0.1) instead of the workspace's Claude pane
        --from STEP                  resume: start again at this step
        --extra-attempts N           resume, reject: add N to the run's attempt allowance when it has spent max_attempts (ignored by a resume that starts no attempt)
        --extra-tokens N             resume, reject: add N to the run's token budget when it has used budget.tokens (ignored by a resume that starts no attempt)
        --to STEP                    reject: the step to run again (the gated step, or one before it)
        --step STEP                  approve, reject: the gated step you saw (current.step in status --json); refused unless the run waits there
        --attempt N                  approve, reject: that step's attempt you saw (current.attempt); needs --step
        --note-sha256 HEX            approve: the sha256 of the gate's note you read (gate_file.sha256); refused with stale_revision when it changed
        --script FILE                simulate: the YAML script of what the fake agent does on each attempt and how each check comes out
        --source                     show ID: the file's text, sha256 of its bytes and problems, valid or not; install: only the source at position N of workflows.sources (a whole number from 1, written after the flag)
        --attempt-of STEP            attempts, audit: only this step's attempts
        --by GROUP                   compare: group the runs by definition (default) or pack:NAME, the text of that pack their agent was sent
        --last DURATION              stats, compare: only runs started in the last DURATION (30d, 2w, 12h, 90m; a run that started exactly then counts)
        --since N                    events: only events after line N of the history (default 0)
        --id ID                      validate: check the text as this workflow id
        --project [NAME]             status: all runs of a project, finished too (NAME, or the project of the current workspace)
        --all                        status: every workspace's runs, finished too
        --needs-me                   status: the runs still going, in every workspace, that wait for you (a gate, question, prompt, failed check, gone pane, stall), each with the next command; --name or --project narrows it
        --table                      status: one row per run with its workspace's status and whether its config, tmux session, worktree and state directory exist; finished runs show at every scope
        --ref REF                    start: run the workflow that fits REF's kind (workflows.by_ref.<kind>, then workflows.default, else the one that fits) instead of naming an ID
        --force                      start: start although the workflow's applies_to: does not list the REF's kind
        --dry-run                    run, start: report what would start and start nothing; sweep: report what would be done and do nothing (also --install and --uninstall); add, update: check and write no definition (the lock file may be created); remove: check and delete nothing
        --install                    sweep: install the launchd entry that runs the sweep every 5 minutes (a per-user LaunchAgent; opt-in)
        --uninstall                  sweep: unload and remove that launchd entry
        --installed                  sweep: say whether that launchd entry is installed and loaded
        --yes                        remove, uninstall: do not ask before deleting
        --if-sha256 SHA              update: the sha256 of the file's raw bytes you read; refuse with stale_workflow unless it still matches
        --prompt TEXT                start: the task as free text (the workflow's task input, and the branch's name when there is no REF)
        --branch BRANCH              start: the branch for a --prompt (default: the prompt's words); refused with a REF
        --slug                       start: add the ticket title's words to a JIRA or issue branch, as `workspace start --slug`
        --base REF                   start: the branch or ref a new branch starts from
        --[no-]headless              start: start the session in plain tmux, as `workspace start --headless`
        --agent-kind KIND            start: the coding agent the main agent pane runs: claude, codex, opencode, pi
        --prompt-timeout DURATION    start: how long to wait for the coding agent to be ready (default 60s)
        --turn-ended                 advance: a turn ended in the run's pane
        --turn-started AT            advance: when that turn began (ISO 8601)
        --stopped-at AT              advance: when the daemon saw that turn end (ISO 8601)
        --background-task TYPE:ID    advance: a background task still going when the turn ended (repeatable)
        --json                       Print one JSON document (see docs/README.workflow.md)
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace workflow show    # list the workflows you can run
  workspace workflow show rpiv    # see the inputs and steps of one before running it
  workspace workflow run rpiv --input task="PROJ-101 invoice PDF export" --dry-run    # check a run in this workspace and start nothing
  workspace workflow run rpiv --input task="PROJ-101 invoice PDF export"    # start it for real: step one is typed into the Claude pane
  workspace workflow start rpiv --prompt "add a hello script"    # make a worktree workspace from a sentence and run rpiv in it
  workspace workflow status    # which runs are going, and why one is stuck
  workspace workflow approve RUN --note "Skip the migration."    # pass the gate a run waits at
  workspace workflow reject RUN --note "Too big; split it."    # send the gated step back with a reason
  workspace workflow resume RUN --from implement    # start a stuck run again at one step
  workspace workflow cancel RUN    # end a run and release its locks
--- end
